## Summary
Document the ownership model and the expected show/hide behavior for the Gym SLL demo.

## User impact
Contributors can follow the documented pattern instead of adding more ad hoc chrome visibility logic.

## Minimal End-to-End Slice
- **Code**: No runtime code beyond doc-snippet consistency checks.
- **Tests**: Ensure any referenced commands or snippets match the real test targets.
- **Docs**: Update `example-games/gym/README.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` with ownership/visibility guidance.
- **Infra**: Reuse the existing docs structure.
- **Observability**: Document how to confirm visibility behavior in the browser demo.

## Existing implementation to reuse
- Gym SLL sections in `example-games/gym/README.md`
- SLL guidance in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
- browser tests for the Gym demo

## Acceptance Criteria
- Docs explain which mode shows which chrome.
- Docs explain how to register objects as shell-owned or scene-owned.
- Docs mention that Scene-only suppresses shared shell chrome.
- Documentation changes match the implemented behavior.

Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

# Fix `worklog_dir_flag` worktree resolution for worktrees under `<main>/.worklog/worktrees`

> **Provenance:** `discovered-from:CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY` (TCE worktree
> `wl-CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY-retire-legacy-choice-fields-and-the-clar`, commit
> `4975f6ff`), observed while running
> `render_report.py CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY` from that worktree.

## Problem statement

`shared/status_lifecycle._detect_worklog_dir()` builds ancestor candidates as
`parent / ".worklog"` for **every** parent, so when the cwd sits inside
`<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` the ancestor `<main>/.worklog`
itself yields `<main>/.worklog/.worklog`; it also accepts any `.worklog`
directory **without** checking that it is initialised. Both defects make
`worklog_dir_flag()` hand `wl` a store root that is either non-existent
(no-op flag) or uninitialised (`wl` fails with
`"Worklog system is not initialized"`), so skill scripts that shell out to
`wl` break when run from an `implement.py` worktree.

## Users

- **AI agent running skill scripts from an implement worktree** — `/skill:report`,
  `/skill:audit`, `persist_audit.py`, and status/lifecycle helpers all resolve
  the store through `worklog_dir_flag()` / `resolve_worklog_flags()`.
  Story: *As an agent finishing work in a worktree, `render_report.py <id>`
  must read the main checkout's worklog so my report is populated and my
  status transition is written to the store the producer reads.*
- **Producer / operator** — needs a trustworthy store resolution so a run from
  a worktree cannot silently target a wrong or uninitialised store.
  Story: *As the producer, when an agent reports from a worktree, the item it
  reports on must be the item in the main checkout's store, with no manual
  `--worklog-dir` correction.*
- **Skill maintainer** — needs the resolution rule pinned by tests.
  Story: *As a skill maintainer, I need a regression test for the
  `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/…` layout so a future refactor of the ancestor
  walk cannot reintroduce a nested `.worklog/.worklog` path.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — worktree root resolves to the main checkout store.**
      With cwd = `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` and no `.worklog`
      in the worktree, `worklog_dir_flag()` returns
      `["--worklog-dir", "<main>/.worklog"]` (the initialised store), including
      when a stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` directory exists.
- [ ] **AC2 — no double suffix.** An ancestor directory already named
      `.worklog` is never extended to `.worklog/.worklog`; the worklog
      directory that is itself an ancestor is the candidate.
- [ ] **AC3 — initialised candidates only.** A candidate `.worklog` that is not
      initialised (`_is_initialized_worklog()` false — e.g. a worktree's
      committed `config.yaml`-only copy) is never returned; resolution
      continues to the nearest initialised ancestor, and returns `[]` (no flag)
      rather than an uninitialised path when nothing initialised exists.
- [ ] **AC4 — unit tests cover the worktree layouts.** New hermetic tests
      (tmp_path fixtures, no real `git worktree`, no network) covering:
      (a) `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` with a stale
      `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` present;
      (b) a **subdirectory** of a worktree whose committed `.worklog/` holds
      only `config.yaml` (the uninitialised-candidate case);
      (c) a plain nested project cwd (no `.worklog` between cwd and the project
      root) still resolving as today (no regression).
- [ ] **AC5 — existing precedence preserved, no weakening.** Precedence
      `explicit --worklog-dir` > prefix-to-sibling scan > cwd chain > no flag is
      unchanged, and the existing tests in
      `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` pass without
      edits to their assertions.
- [ ] **AC6 — documentation.** The resolution rule (initialised-only, no
      `.worklog/.worklog` nesting, worktree-ancestor special case) is stated in
      the code docstrings of `_detect_worklog_dir()` / `worklog_dir_flag()` and
      in `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (the section that says
      `StatusLifecycle` resolves the worklog dir automatically) and
      `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` (the worklog-store resolution note).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo location.** The defective code lives in the **SorraAgents**
  repository (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`); `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a
  symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill` and the TCE checkout
  carries no `skill/` tree. Where the fix and its record land is an **open
  producer decision** (Appendix Q1). Do **not** edit the TCE project-local
  `.pi/`, and do not create a vendored copy of the helper.
- **Shared seam.** `status_lifecycle` is imported by every skill; keep the
  change narrow (one candidate-selection helper reused by both
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` and `worklog_dir_flag()`), with no behaviour change
  for cwds that already resolve correctly.
- **Fail closed, never guess.** Returning no `--worklog-dir` (so `wl` reports
  the real error) is preferred over returning a path that is not an initialised
  store.
- **Hermetic tests.** No real `git worktree`/network in the unit tests;
  `unittest.mock.patch` on `Path.cwd`-derived inputs or `tmp_path` layouts,
  matching the existing test module's style.
- **Gate order.** build → test → commit, never reversed; no ad-hoc `pytest` —
  run tests through the test skill (`/skill:test` / `run_tests.py`).

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- Source of truth: `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills` → `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill`).
- `_detect_worklog_dir()` (line ~258) order: `<cwd>/.worklog` →
  `<git toplevel>/.worklog` → `for parent in cwd.parents: parent/".worklog"`;
  the last two gates call `is_dir()` only, never `_is_initialized_worklog()`.
- `worklog_dir_flag()` (line ~391) has a **second, different** ancestor walk
  that *does* check `_is_initialized_worklog()`, then falls back to
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` — so the two walks disagree.
- Reproduced (TCE, registered worktree, git toplevel = the worktree):
  ```
  cwd=/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/worktrees/wl-CG-0MRBDPFPH009Y8M0-balance-tooling
  _detect_worklog_dir() -> /home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/.worklog
  worklog_dir_flag()    -> ['--worklog-dir', '…/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/.worklog']
  ```
  The stale `…/.worklog/.worklog/` exists and contains only a `worktrees/`
  subdirectory (no `initialized` marker, no `worklog.db`).
- Reproduced (SorraAgents, registered worktree, run from a **subdirectory** so
  the `cwd/.worklog` branch is skipped):
  ```
  cwd=…/.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSQ8MXXI0029B5M-…/skill
  _detect_worklog_dir() -> <that worktree>/.worklog      # config.yaml only — NOT initialised
  worklog_dir_flag()    -> ['--worklog-dir', '<worktree>/.worklog']
  ```
  i.e. a second manifestation of the same defect (uninitialised candidate),
  at the worktree **root** even though the initialised main store is a direct
  ancestor. Both are in scope via AC1–AC3.
- `_resolve_repo_root()` already handles the worktree case for the framework
  root (`tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py::TestFrameworkRootDerivation`)
  — the framework root is correct; only the *store* resolution is wrong.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` covers prefix scan,
  `resolve_worklog_dir`, `resolve_worklog_flags` precedence and `run_wl`
  injection, but has **no** ancestor-walk / worktree-layout test.
- `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` re-uses `worklog_dir_flag()`, so it is fixed
  transitively. `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` resolves its own target
  project root and is unaffected.
- Adjacent same-class defect (out of scope unless Appendix Q2 says otherwise):
  `skill/shared/code_freeze.py::_detect_worklog_dir()` (line ~48) duplicates the
  ancestor walk with the same `parent/".worklog"` construction and no
  initialisation check, so `code_freeze_marker_path()` would read
  `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/code-freeze.json` from a worktree.

## Desired change

1. Introduce one candidate-selection helper used by both
   `_detect_worklog_dir()` and `worklog_dir_flag()`:
   - for each ancestor, if the ancestor **is** a worklog directory
     (`name == ".worklog"`), the candidate is that ancestor itself; otherwise
     the candidate is `ancestor / ".worklog"`;
   - only accept a candidate when `_is_initialized_worklog(candidate)` is true
     (in the `_detect_worklog_dir` gate; `worklog_dir_flag` keeps its existing
     "no flag" contract when nothing initialised is found).
2. Delete the duplicated walk in `worklog_dir_flag()` in favour of the shared
   helper (no second, divergent rule).
3. Tests per AC4, in the existing
   `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` module style.
4. Doc updates per AC6.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (SorraAgents) — `_detect_worklog_dir()`
  (~line 258) gains the `.worklog`-named-ancestor rule and the
  `_is_initialized_worklog()` gate; `worklog_dir_flag()` (~line 391) re-uses the
  same helper instead of its own walk; docstrings per AC6.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` (SorraAgents) — new
  `TestWorklogDirAncestorWalk` class with the AC4 cases.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (SorraAgents) — the "`StatusLifecycle`
  resolves the same directory automatically" paragraph (~lines 84–88) gains the
  initialised-only / no-nesting rule.
- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` (SorraAgents) — worklog-store resolution
  note (~lines 360–364).
- `skill/shared/code_freeze.py` (SorraAgents) — **only if** Appendix Q2 answer
  folds the adjacent defect in; otherwise unchanged and filed separately.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL` (open, intake_complete) — *implement.py finish reports
  status changes that the main worklog store does not show*. Same seam, wider
  scope (finish must pass an explicit store). Its "Existing state" note claims
  `worklog_dir_flag` "does resolve the main checkout store from a worktree";
  the evidence above shows that holds only when no stale
  `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` exists — this item carries the counter-example.
  Partial overlap only, so **not** a duplicate.
- `CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY` (TCE) — discovery work item (`discovered-from`).
- `CG-0MUC5GVCJ0062BN7` (TCE, completed) — earlier worktree-resolution defect
  (`.pi/test-config.json` unseen from a worktree): same failure family,
  different file.
- `SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51`, `SA-0MSGH55OJ003WKYZ`, `SA-0MTOMCML900254CI`
  (completed) — the prefix-to-sibling seam and cwd-independence lineage this
  item extends.
- Automated `find-related` report (TCE-scoped) is appended to this
  description; it surfaced no overlapping TCE code, so the cross-store search
  above was done manually.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: resolver regression elsewhere.** Other skills rely on
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` returning a non-initialised directory in exotic
  layouts. Mitigation: AC5 requires the existing suite to pass unchanged; the
  change only *narrows* accepted candidates, and `worklog_dir_flag()` keeps its
  "no flag" fallback so `wl` still reports its own error.
- **Risk: `.worklog`-named ancestor inside a normal project** (e.g. a directory
  literally called `.worklog` used for something else). Mitigation: the
  `.worklog`-named ancestor is only accepted when `_is_initialized_worklog()`
  is true.
- **Risk: styling split between the two walks** if only one is fixed.
  Mitigation: single shared helper (Desired change 1–2).
- **Scope-creep risk: fixing `code_freeze.py` in the same change.** Recorded as
  Appendix Q2; default is a separate `discovered-from` item so this fix stays
  narrow.
- **Assumption:** the "stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog`" directory is a local
  artefact (from an old run) and is not committed anywhere; the fix must not
  depend on its removal, because the nesting rule is wrong regardless.
- **Assumption:** unit tests can express the layout with `tmp_path` +
  `mock.patch` rather than creating real git worktrees (the existing module
  already models the framework-root worktree layout this way).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (OPEN QUESTION, producer input required) — Where should the fix and its
  record land?** The defective code is in the SorraAgents repo
  (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`); the TCE checkout has no `skill/` tree,
  so a TCE `implement.py` worktree cannot carry the change and
  `implement.py finish` fails closed on out-of-worktree edits. Options:
  (a) transfer this item to the SA store and close the CG item as transferred
  (precedent: `SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL`, transferred from `OSL-0MVFHAT31007ZILJ` by
  operator decision);
  (b) create an SA item carrying the code + tests and keep this CG item as the
  discovery/tracking record (linked both ways);
  (c) keep it in CG and commit to SorraAgents `dev` from outside a TCE worktree
  (breaks the worktree-isolation gate).
  **Recommended: (b)** — it preserves TCE provenance, keeps the SA store as the
  record for SA-owned code, and lets the change pass SA's Python test gate.
  Answer: _(pending — no producer response yet)_.
- **Q2 (OPEN QUESTION, producer input required) — Fold in the adjacent
  `code_freeze.py` defect?** `skill/shared/code_freeze.py::_detect_worklog_dir()`
  duplicates the same walk (`.worklog/.worklog` risk, no initialisation check),
  so the code-freeze marker can be read from the wrong directory.
  Options: (a) fix both in this change (one shared helper, slightly wider diff);
  (b) keep this item narrow and file the `code_freeze` fix as a separate
  `discovered-from` item.
  **Recommended: (b)** — surgical change first; the adjacent fix is recorded
  rather than smuggled in. Answer: _(pending — no producer response yet)_.
- **Q3 — Duplicate-work check (agent-resolved).** Searched both stores
  (`worklog_dir_flag`, `worktree resolution`, `nested worklog dir`) —
  `SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL` is the only overlapping item and its ACs do not cover
  the nesting/initialisation defects, so no duplicate close or rewrite was
  applied; it is cross-referenced in *Related work*. Answer: **no full
  duplicate; partial overlap cross-linked.**
data.title: Fix worklog_dir_flag worktree resolution for worktrees under <main>/.worklog/worktrees

# Game-repo scaffold and `install_pi.sh` must wire git hooks and emit a full-suite pre-push variant

discovered-from: MS-0MVTI7F5R009OQ14 (tce-main-street)

## Problem statement

Game repos generated from the engine scaffold (`core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) receive a committed `.githooks/` directory but **no activation**: the scaffold never sets `core.hooksPath`, so git ignores the committed hooks in every fresh clone until someone runs `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` by hand. `scripts/install_pi.sh` is the documented wiring path, but it only acts when run interactively inside the project, and it deliberately gives non-SorraAgents projects the **v2** hook — branch policy + context-budget gate + worklog sync, with **no full-suite test gate**.

Consequence for every `tce-<game>` repo: `implement.py finish` defers full-suite testing to "the dev-push gate — the pre-push hook executes `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env`", but no such step exists in the hook it wires. A red tree can be pushed straight to `dev`, no gate-produced full-suite cache entry exists for the audit skill to reuse, and the context-budget gate is fail-open because per-project thresholds files are not generated at scaffold time.

Verified in `tce-main-street` (2026-11-03): `core.hooksPath` unset; `.githooks/pre-push` is v2 byte-for-byte; `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` absent; `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` contains no `githooks`/`hooksPath` wiring at all.

## Users / user stories

- As a **game producer/agent**, I want a freshly scaffolded (or freshly cloned) game repo to have active git hooks, so branch policy, worklog sync and the context-budget gate work without a manual per-clone step.
- As the **producer**, I want the documented dev-push full-suite gate to actually run in game repos, so "pushed to `dev`" means "green at this git state" and the audit skill can reuse a real cache entry.
- As a **framework maintainer**, I want one hook variant that works without a repo-local `skill/` tree, so the gate does not hard-fail (v3 today) or silently no-op (v2 today) in game repos.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Scaffold wires hooks and thresholds.** `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` sets `core.hooksPath=.githooks` for generated repos, installs the selected pre-push hook, and generates/commits `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` from the new repo's measured surface. *Metric: scaffold a throwaway repo in a temp dir, then assert `git config --get core.hooksPath` is `.githooks`, `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` resolves inside `.githooks`, and the thresholds file exists and passes `measure_context.py`.*
- **AC2 — Game-repo full-suite hook variant.** A committed template (e.g. `.githooks/pre-push.game` or a v4 unified hook) adds the scope-aware test gate to the current v2 content: read push refs once, run the full suite only for `refs/heads/dev`/`refs/heads/main`, fail the push on a non-zero exit, skip tests for feature branches, and run the gate **before** the worktree worklog early-exit. The runner resolves `$repo_root/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` when present, otherwise the installed global `$HOME/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py` with `--project-root "$repo_root"`; absent both, fail closed for `dev`/`main` with an actionable message. `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` bypasses. *Metric: end-to-end tests drive the hook with stub runners — failing stub on a `dev` push exits non-zero, passing stub exits 0, a feature-branch push never invokes the runner, a missing runner fails closed.*
- **AC3 — `install_pi.sh` selects the game variant.** The hook selection chooses the full-suite variant when there is no repo-local runner but a global runner is available (or unconditionally for `tce-*` game repos), keeps the existing idempotence rules (never overwrite a foreign hook, `PI_SKIP_HOOK_INSTALL=1` opt-out), and updates the resulting table in `docs/dev/context-budget.md` (SorraAgents v3/v4, game repos full-suite variant, other projects v2). *Metric: installer tests cover each selection branch and the docs table matches the implementation.*
- **AC4 — Worktree-safe under `--strict-git-env`.** The gate runs successfully from a linked worktree push (git-exported worktree-managed `GIT_DIR` is exempt; see `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9) and from the main checkout. *Metric: an end-to-end test pushes from a linked worktree with the global runner and asserts the suite is invoked and the push is gated; no `--strict-git-env` refusal.*
- **AC5 — Rollout verified in a real game repo and documented.** Re-run the installer against `../tce-main-street`, confirm `core.hooksPath` and the full-suite gate on a real `dev` push (cache entry produced), and update `docs/dev/context-budget.md` plus any scaffold/README notes. The full engine test suite passes with the change.

## Constraints

- Engine/framework change only: no edits to game repos' source; use a game checkout solely as rollout verification (as the AI_Hell v2 rollout did, SA-0MSN2ULOF007JJ35).
- POSIX `sh` hook; no new runtime dependencies; the hook must keep working on a bare git checkout.
- Do not weaken the existing v2 gates (branch policy, context budget, worklog sync) or their bypass variables.
- Keep the gate fail-*closed* for a missing runner on `dev`/`main` (the reason v2 was chosen was the *absence* of a runner, not a preference for skipping); fail-open remains acceptable only for optional tooling (context-budget measurement).
- Preserve `install_pi.sh` idempotence and the `PI_SKIP_HOOK_INSTALL=1` opt-out; never overwrite an existing foreign hook.
- Respect the project test-execution policy: no ad-hoc suite invocation; use the test skill.

## Existing state

- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — no `githooks`/`hooksPath` handling (grep returns nothing).
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — hook wiring block picks `.githooks/pre-push` (v3) only when `$repo_root/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` exists, else `.githooks/pre-push.v2`; sets `core.hooksPath=.githooks`; warns when per-project thresholds are missing.
- `.githooks/pre-push` (v3) — SorraAgents variant with `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env`, hard-fails when the runner is absent.
- `.githooks/pre-push.v2` — framework variant for non-runner projects (branch policy + context budget + worklog sync).
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` — documents both variants, the rollout table and the "new projects via install_pi.sh" mechanics; must be updated with any third variant.
- Evidence repo: `../tce-main-street` (game) — v2 hook active only via an unversioned `.git/hooks` copy, no thresholds file, no full-suite step.

## Desired change

1. Add the full-suite gate to a game-repo hook variant (single unified v4 template is acceptable if it resolves an optional runner the same way), keeping v2's ordering and bypasses.
2. Wire hook activation and thresholds generation into the game-repo scaffold so new repos need no manual step.
3. Teach `install_pi.sh` to select the variant for projects without a repo-local runner and to generate the thresholds file (or print the exact command and fail loudly if `--generate-thresholds` is not possible).
4. Add end-to-end hook/installer/scaffold tests (stub runners, temp repos, linked worktree).
5. Update `docs/dev/context-budget.md` (variant table, rollout, troubleshooting) and the scaffold/README notes; then verify the rollout in `tce-main-street`.
6. Remove or supersede the v2-vs-v3 split rationale once the unified variant is chosen (do not leave stale docs claiming game repos cannot have the gate).

## Key Files

- `.githooks/pre-push.game` (new) or `.githooks/pre-push` (extended) — full-suite variant with optional global-runner resolution.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — variant selection, thresholds generation, idempotence and opt-out preserved.
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — set `core.hooksPath`, install the hook, seed the thresholds file.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` — variant/rollout table and mechanics.
- `tests/test_pre_push_context_budget_gate.py` — extend with full-suite gate ordering/fail-closed cases (or add a sibling hook test).
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` (or the existing scaffold suite location) — assert hook wiring + thresholds generation.
- `tests/test_install_pi_hook_selection.py` (new or existing installer suite) — assert variant selection branches.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVTI7F5R009OQ14** — `tce-main-street` git hooks inactivity (open): game-side repair of this checkout; producer deferred the full-suite gate and scaffold wiring to this engine item (answers Q1=c, Q3=a).
- **SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM** — original reason non-SorraAgents projects get the v2 hook (they lack `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`); this item supersedes that constraint by resolving the global runner.
- **SA-0MSN2ULOF007JJ35** — AI_Hell v2 rollout: precedent for wiring a real project and verifying the gate end-to-end.
- **SA-0MT6CEN8D0073F61 / SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81** — scope-aware test gate and the "full suite first runs at the dev-push gate" deferral this item makes real for game repos.
- **SA-0MT1WUEIT006U1HC** — automated hook wiring via `install_pi.sh`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — hook blocks every game push.** A bug in runner resolution would stop all `dev` pushes. Mitigate with end-to-end stub-runner tests, `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`, and an explicit fail-closed message naming the remedy.
- **Risk — suite duration at push time.** A game full suite is minutes (e.g. `tce-main-street` ≈ 3–4 min plus two serial browser suites). Acceptable at one `dev` push per work item; the runner cache makes repeat pushes cheap.
- **Risk — host-wide test-slot contention** when a hook holds the runner's lock. Document the behaviour; rely on the runner's own bounded lock timeout.
- **Assumption — global runner availability.** Game-machine installs include the test skill (`~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`); the hook's fail-closed message must name `install_pi.sh` when it is missing.
- **Assumption — scaffold regeneration is safe.** Setting `core.hooksPath` is local config, so the scaffold must document that re-cloning still needs one activation step (or `install_pi.sh`).
- **Scope-creep risk:** porting every game repo now, or redesigning the context-budget measurement, is out of scope; one rollout repo proves the path.
